revealWordProblem.title: Apply: The Evidence Locker
revealWordProblem.text: Detective Chen logs evidence bags into the agency vault. After she adds 18 new bags from today's case, the vault holds 64 bags in all. The equation b + 18 = 64 shows the situation, where b is the number of bags that were already in the vault. How many evidence bags were in the vault before today?
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Subtract 18 from both sides: b = 64 − 18 = 46. There were 46 evidence bags in the vault before today. Check: 46 + 18 = 64 ✓

conceptIntro.heading: Push further — How do I solve an addition or subtraction equation?
conceptIntro.intro: You already can do this. So we go up a level, not up a number: find what is always true, show it a second way, and be ready to defend it with a reason instead of an answer.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: Undo the operation with its inverse, and do it to both sides to keep the equation balanced — and you can say why it is true, and where it would stop being true.

iDo.title: Watch me
lines: Solve n + 23 = 58. The 23 is added to n.
The inverse of adding 23 is subtracting 23.
I subtract 23 from both sides: n + 23 − 23 = 58 − 23.
linesEs: Resuelve n + 23 = 58. El 23 se le suma a n.
La inversa de sumar 23 es restar 23.
Resto 23 en los dos lados: n + 23 − 23 = 58 − 23.

weDo.title: Try it together — then prove it
lines: Solve x − 4 = 9. Is x being added or subtracted?
It is subtracted, so the inverse is adding 4 to both sides.
Now prove it: say why that move had to work at all — not just that it did.
Sentence frame — convince a skeptic: "My method works because ___ . It would stop working if ___ ."
linesEs: Resuelve x − 4 = 9. ¿A x se le está sumando o restando?
Se le está restando, así que la inversa es sumar 4 en los dos lados.
Ahora demuéstralo: di por qué ese paso tenía que funcionar — no solo que funcionó.
Marco de oración — convence a alguien que duda: «Mi método funciona porque ___ . Dejaría de funcionar si ___ .»

youDo.title: Now you try — and defend it
lines: Try the problems below on your own. Getting the answer is half the work — be ready to say why your method works, and where it would stop working.
Then pick one problem and show it a second way. If two different methods agree, that agreement is your proof.
linesEs: Intenta los problemas de abajo por tu cuenta. Obtener la respuesta es la mitad del trabajo — prepárate para decir por qué funciona tu método y dónde dejaría de funcionar.
Luego elige un problema y muéstralo de una segunda manera. Si dos métodos distintos coinciden, esa coincidencia es tu prueba.

conceptIntro.headingEs: Ve más allá — ¿Cómo resuelvo una ecuación de suma o de resta?
conceptIntro.introEs: Esto ya lo sabes hacer. Así que subimos de nivel, no de número: halla lo que siempre es cierto, muéstralo de una segunda manera y prepárate para defenderlo con una razón en lugar de una respuesta.
conceptIntro.keyIdeaEs: Deshaz la operación con su inversa, y hazlo en los dos lados para mantener la ecuación equilibrada — y puedes decir por qué es cierto y dónde dejaría de serlo.

explore.instructions: Go deeper: Use the balance scale to solve n + 19 = 46. What must you do to both sides to isolate n? As you work, ask yourself WHY it works.
hints: To isolate n, you need to remove the +19. What is the inverse of adding 19?
Subtract 19 from BOTH sides: n + 19 − 19 = 46 − 19 → n = 27.
explore.label: Solve the equation using the balance scale. Keep both sides equal!

discourse.prompt: Why do you have to subtract 19 from BOTH sides, not just one?
discourse.sentenceFrame: I subtract from both sides because an equation is like a ___ — to keep it balanced, any operation on one side must ___.

onLevel.stem: A shirt costs $d. After a $15 discount, it costs $38. What is d?
choiceFeedback: That is what you get if you subtracted 15 from 38. Instead: d − 15 = 38 → d = 38 + 15 = $53.
That is the price after the discount, not the original price. The original price has to be larger, so add the discount back on.
The discount was not added back fully. Set up d − 15 = 38, then add 15 to both sides and combine carefully.
hints: The $15 discount was taken OFF the original price d, and $38 is what's left after the discount.
Write the story first: d − 15 = 38. Then undo the subtraction — the original price should be MORE than $38, not less.
Add the $15 discount back onto the $38 sale price: d = 38 + 15. Which choice matches that total?
onLevel.stemEs: Una camisa cuesta $d. Después de un descuento de $15, cuesta $38. ¿Cuánto vale d?
hintsEs: El descuento de $15 se le QUITÓ al precio original d, y $38 es lo que queda después del descuento.
Escribe primero la historia: d − 15 = 38. Luego deshaz la resta: el precio original debe ser MÁS de $38, no menos.
Vuelve a sumar los $15 del descuento al precio de oferta de $38: d = 38 + 15. ¿Qué opción coincide con ese total?

onLevel.title: Spot the Common Mistake

workedExample.label: Choose inverse
workedExample.work: The inverse of − 13 is + 13, so add 13 to both sides.
workedExample.workEs: La inversa de − 13 es + 13, así que suma 13 a ambos lados.

onLevel.correctWork: The inverse operation was correct, but the addition was done wrong: 28 + 13 = 41, not 31. So y = 41. Check: 41 − 13 = 28 ✓
hints: The plan (add 13 to both sides) is right. Recheck the arithmetic in the last step.
Add carefully: 28 + 13 = 41, so y = 41, not 31.
onLevel.explanation: The plan was correct — adding 13 to both sides is the right inverse for y − 13 = 28 — but the "Simplify" step adds wrong. 28 + 13 = 41, not 31, so y = 41. Substituting back confirms it: 41 − 13 = 28, while 31 − 13 would give 18.
onLevel.explanationEs: El plan era correcto —sumar 13 en ambos lados es la inversa adecuada para y − 13 = 28—, pero el paso "Simplify" suma mal. 28 + 13 = 41, no 31, así que y = 41. Sustituir de regreso lo confirma: 41 − 13 = 28, mientras que 31 − 13 daría 18.
onLevel.correctWorkEs: La operación inversa era correcta, pero la suma se hizo mal: 28 + 13 = 41, no 31. Así que y = 41. Comprueba: 41 − 13 = 28 ✓
hintsEs: El plan (sumar 13 a ambos lados) está bien. Vuelve a revisar la aritmética del último paso.
Suma con cuidado: 28 + 13 = 41, así que y = 41, no 31.

onLevel.title: Find the Equation Error

workedExample.label: Identify inverse
workedExample.workEs: La inversa de la resta es la resta

onLevel.correctWork: Inverse of subtraction is ADDITION. Add 18 to both sides: x = 45 + 18 = 63.
hints: Step 2 says the inverse of subtraction is subtraction. Is that right?
To undo −18, you need +18, not another −18. Addition undoes subtraction.
onLevel.titleEs: Encuentra el error de la ecuación
onLevel.explanation: The "Identify inverse" step claims subtraction undoes subtraction, which pushes the equation further from the answer instead of isolating x. Addition undoes subtraction, so add 18 to both sides of x − 18 = 45: x = 45 + 18 = 63. Checking, 63 − 18 = 45, while the answer 27 would give 9.
onLevel.explanationEs: El paso "Identify inverse" afirma que la resta deshace la resta, lo que aleja la ecuación de la respuesta en lugar de despejar x. La suma deshace la resta, así que suma 18 en ambos lados de x − 18 = 45: x = 45 + 18 = 63. Al comprobar, 63 − 18 = 45, mientras que la respuesta 27 daría 9.
onLevel.correctWorkEs: La inversa de la resta es la SUMA. Suma 18 a ambos lados: x = 45 + 18 = 63.
hintsEs: El Paso 2 dice que la operación inversa de la resta es la resta. ¿Es correcto?
Para deshacer −18, necesitas +18, no otro −18. La suma deshace la resta.

onLevel.prompt: A detective solved x + 25 = 60 and got x = 35. Another detective solved y − 25 = 60 and got y = 35. Are both correct? Explain using inverse operations and check each answer.
onLevel.sentenceFrame: For x + 25 = 60, the inverse operation is ___, so x = ___. Check: ___. For y − 25 = 60, the inverse operation is ___, so y = ___. Check: ___. Therefore, ___.
onLevel.hint: Use a strategy or example from the lesson to help you explain your answer.
hints: The two equations use OPPOSITE operations (+25 and −25), so the same inverse step cannot work for both.
Solve each with its own inverse: subtract 25 for x + 25 = 60, but add 25 for y − 25 = 60. Then substitute each result back into its equation.
Start with x + 25 = 60: subtract 25 from both sides and compare with the detective's 35. Then add 25 for the y equation and see whether 35 survives that check.
onLevel.explanation: Only the first detective is right. For x + 25 = 60 the inverse is subtraction, so x = 60 − 25 = 35, and 35 + 25 = 60 checks out. For y − 25 = 60 the inverse is addition, so y = 60 + 25 = 85, not 35 — substituting 35 gives 35 − 25 = 10, not 60. Opposite operations need opposite inverses, even when the numbers look identical.
onLevel.explanationEs: Solo el primer detective tiene razón. Para x + 25 = 60 la inversa es la resta, así que x = 60 − 25 = 35, y 35 + 25 = 60 comprueba bien. Para y − 25 = 60 la inversa es la suma, así que y = 60 + 25 = 85, no 35: al sustituir 35 da 35 − 25 = 10, no 60. Operaciones opuestas necesitan inversas opuestas, aunque los números se vean idénticos.
onLevel.promptEs: Un detective resolvió x + 25 = 60 y obtuvo x = 35. Otra detective resolvió y − 25 = 60 y obtuvo y = 35. ¿Están los dos correctos? Explica usando operaciones inversas y comprueba cada respuesta.
hintsEs: Las dos ecuaciones usan operaciones OPUESTAS (+25 y −25), así que el mismo paso inverso no puede servir para ambas.
Resuelve cada una con su propia inversa: resta 25 en x + 25 = 60, pero suma 25 en y − 25 = 60. Luego sustituye cada resultado en su ecuación.
Empieza con x + 25 = 60: resta 25 de ambos lados y compara con el 35 del detective. Luego suma 25 en la ecuación de y y ve si el 35 sobrevive esa prueba.

extending.label: Solve: m − 14 = 32
hints: The inverse of subtracting 14 is adding 14.
Add 14 to both sides: m = 32 + 14 = 46.
extending.explanation: In m − 14 = 32 the variable has 14 taken away from it, so add 14 to both sides to undo that: m = 32 + 14 = 46. Checking keeps the scale balanced, since 46 − 14 = 32.
extending.explanationEs: En m − 14 = 32 a la variable se le quitan 14, así que suma 14 en ambos lados para deshacerlo: m = 32 + 14 = 46. La comprobación mantiene la balanza equilibrada, ya que 46 − 14 = 32.
hintsEs: La operación inversa de restar 14 es sumar 14.
Suma 14 a ambos lados: m = 32 + 14 = 46.

extending.label: Complete the table: identify the inverse operation, solve, and check.
extending.hint: Work through each row step by step, checking your answer after each one.
hints: Every row asks the same three things: what is being done to the variable, how do you undo it, and does the check rebuild the original equation?
If the equation ADDS a number, the inverse is subtract; if it SUBTRACTS, the inverse is add. Always do it to both sides — decimals like 3.5 follow the same rule.
Row 1: x + 18 = 45 adds 18, so subtract 18 from both sides and compute 45 − 18. Verify by adding 18 back, then move to row 2.
extending.explanation: Each row names what is done to the variable, then undoes it on both sides. x + 18 = 45 adds 18, so subtract 18: x = 27, and 27 + 18 = 45. p − 22 = 19 subtracts 22, so add 22: p = 41, and 41 − 22 = 19. w + 3.5 = 10 adds 3.5, so subtract 3.5: w = 6.5, and 6.5 + 3.5 = 10 — decimals follow exactly the same rule.
extending.explanationEs: Cada fila nombra lo que se le hace a la variable y luego lo deshace en ambos lados. x + 18 = 45 suma 18, así que resta 18: x = 27, y 27 + 18 = 45. p − 22 = 19 resta 22, así que suma 22: p = 41, y 41 − 22 = 19. w + 3.5 = 10 suma 3.5, así que resta 3.5: w = 6.5, y 6.5 + 3.5 = 10; los decimales siguen exactamente la misma regla.
extending.labelEs: Completa la tabla: identifica la operación inversa, resuelve y comprueba.
hintsEs: Cada fila pide las mismas tres cosas: qué se le hace a la variable, cómo lo deshaces y si la comprobación reconstruye la ecuación original.
Si la ecuación SUMA un número, la inversa es restar; si RESTA, la inversa es sumar. Hazlo siempre en ambos lados: los decimales como 3.5 siguen la misma regla.
Fila 1: x + 18 = 45 suma 18, así que resta 18 de ambos lados y calcula 45 − 18. Verifica sumando 18 de nuevo y pasa a la fila 2.

extending.explanation: Subtract 7 from both sides: x = 15 − 7 = 8. Check: 8 + 7 = 15 ✓
choiceFeedback: Not quite. Subtract 7 from both sides: x = 15 − 7 = ___.
That is the number being added in the equation, not the unknown value. Subtract it from both sides to uncover x.
The two numbers got multiplied. Addition is undone by subtraction, so take 7 away from both sides instead.
extending.explanationEs: Resta 7 en ambos lados: x = 15 − 7 = 8. Comprueba: 8 + 7 = 15 ✓
hints: The equation shows something being added to x, and the equal sign means both sides have the same value.
Use the inverse operation: whatever is added to x should be subtracted from both sides.
Subtract 7 from both sides. The left side becomes just x, and the right side becomes 15 − 7 — finish that subtraction.
hintsEs: La ecuación muestra que algo se le suma a x, y el signo igual significa que ambos lados tienen el mismo valor.
Usa la operación inversa: lo que se le suma a x debe restarse en ambos lados.
Resta 7 en ambos lados. El lado izquierdo queda solo como x y el derecho queda como 15 − 7 — termina esa resta.

extending.explanation: Add 4 to both sides: n = 9 + 4 = 13. Check: 13 − 4 = 9 ✓
choiceFeedback: Not quite. Add 4 to both sides: n = 9 + 4 = ___.
The numbers were multiplied instead of combined with the inverse operation. Subtraction is undone by addition, so add 4 to both sides.
The subtraction ran in the wrong direction. Since 4 was taken away from n, n has to be larger than 9 — add 4 to both sides.
extending.explanationEs: Suma 4 en ambos lados: n = 9 + 4 = 13. Comprueba: 13 − 4 = 9 ✓
hints: This equation takes an amount away from n, and you need to find what n was before that happened.
Undo a subtraction with addition, applying it to both sides of the equation.
Add 4 to both sides. The left side becomes just n, and the right side becomes 9 + 4 — finish that addition.
hintsEs: Esta ecuación le quita una cantidad a n, y tienes que hallar cuánto valía n antes de eso.
Deshaz una resta con una suma, aplicándola a ambos lados de la ecuación.
Suma 4 en ambos lados. El lado izquierdo queda solo como n y el derecho queda como 9 + 4 — termina esa suma.

extending.stem: Unlock Card 3: A vault held some clue tokens. After the detective added 16 tokens, there were 50. The equation is t + 16 = 50. How many tokens were there before?
extending.explanation: Subtract 16 from both sides: t = 50 − 16 = 34. Check: 34 + 16 = 50 ✓
choiceFeedback: Not quite. Subtract 16 from both sides: t = 50 − 16 = ___.
That is the number of tokens the detective added, not how many were there before. Subtract 16 from both sides to find the starting amount.
The two numbers got multiplied. Since 16 was added to t, subtract 16 from both sides instead.
extending.stemEs: Tarjeta de desbloqueo 3: Una bóveda tenía algunas fichas de pistas. Después de que el detective agregó 16 fichas, había 50. La ecuación es t + 16 = 50. ¿Cuántas fichas había antes?
extending.explanationEs: Resta 16 en ambos lados: t = 50 − 16 = 34. Comprueba: 34 + 16 = 50 ✓
hints: Tokens were added to a starting amount to reach 50, so the starting amount has to be smaller than 50.
The equation t + 16 = 50 is undone by subtracting 16 from both sides.
Subtract 16 from both sides. The left side leaves just t, and the right side becomes 50 − 16 — finish that subtraction.
hintsEs: Se agregaron fichas a una cantidad inicial hasta llegar a 50, así que la cantidad inicial tiene que ser menor que 50.
La ecuación t + 16 = 50 se deshace restando 16 en ambos lados.
Resta 16 en ambos lados. El lado izquierdo deja solo a t y el derecho queda como 50 − 16 — termina esa resta.

extending.title: Level 2 Extension — Crack the Detective's Mistake
extending.correctWork: To undo + 8 you SUBTRACT 8 from both sides, not add: x + 8 − 8 = 21 − 8, so x = 13. Check: 13 + 8 = 21 ✓
hints: Step 3 adds 8 to both sides. Does adding 8 again remove the + 8?
The inverse of adding 8 is subtracting 8. Subtract 8 from both sides to isolate x.
extending.titleEs: Extensión de Nivel 2 — Descifra el error del detective
extending.explanation: The "Apply to both sides" step adds 8 again, which leaves x + 16 on the left instead of x alone. To undo + 8 you subtract 8 from both sides: x + 8 − 8 = 21 − 8, so x = 13. Checking, 13 + 8 = 21, while x = 29 would give 37.
extending.explanationEs: El paso "Apply to both sides" vuelve a sumar 8, lo que deja x + 16 a la izquierda en lugar de x sola. Para deshacer + 8 restas 8 en ambos lados: x + 8 − 8 = 21 − 8, así que x = 13. Al comprobar, 13 + 8 = 21, mientras que x = 29 daría 37.
extending.correctWorkEs: Para deshacer + 8 debes RESTAR 8 de ambos lados, no sumar: x + 8 − 8 = 21 − 8, así que x = 13. Comprueba: 13 + 8 = 21 ✓
hintsEs: El Paso 3 suma 8 a ambos lados. ¿Sumar 8 otra vez quita el + 8?
La operación inversa de sumar 8 es restar 8. Resta 8 de ambos lados para despejar x.

extending.explanation: Subtract 9 from both sides: x = 15 − 9 = 6. Check: 6 + 9 = 15 ✓
choiceFeedback: Not quite. Subtract 9 from both sides: x = 15 − 9 = ___.
That number is already showing in the equation as the amount being added, not the unknown. Undo the addition by subtracting it from both sides.
That is the total after 9 was added, not the starting value. Work backward from the total by subtracting 9 from both sides.
hints: x has 9 added to it. To get x alone, you need to UNDO that addition.
Use the inverse operation: subtraction undoes addition. Whatever you do, do it to BOTH sides to keep the balance.
Subtract 9 from both sides: x = 15 − 9. Then check by adding 9 back to your result — do you land on 15?
extending.explanationEs: Resta 9 en ambos lados: x = 15 − 9 = 6. Comprueba: 6 + 9 = 15 ✓
hintsEs: A x se le suman 9. Para dejar x sola, tienes que DESHACER esa suma.
Usa la operación inversa: la resta deshace la suma. Lo que hagas, hazlo en AMBOS lados para mantener el equilibrio.
Resta 9 de ambos lados: x = 15 − 9. Luego comprueba sumando 9 de nuevo a tu resultado: ¿llegas a 15?

extending.explanation: Add 7 to both sides: y = 20 + 7 = 27. Check: 27 − 7 = 20 ✓
choiceFeedback: Not quite. Add 7 to both sides: y = 20 + 7 = ___.
That is the amount being subtracted, not the value of y. Undo the subtraction by adding it to both sides.
The two numbers got multiplied. Subtraction is undone by addition, so add 7 to both sides instead.
hints: Look at what's happening to y: 7 is being SUBTRACTED. Which operation undoes subtraction?

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake is applying the same operation instead of the inverse — for example, solving x − 7 = 15 by subtracting 7 from both sides (getting the wrong x = 8) instead of adding 7 to both sides (the correct x = 22). Another common mistake is doing the inverse operation to only one side, like solving x + 6 = 14 by subtracting 6 from the left but forgetting the right side. Before you submit, name the operation shown in the equation, choose its inverse, apply it to BOTH sides, and check by substituting your answer back into the original equation.

diagram.caption: The whole 12-mile trail (top bar) equals the distance walked (d) plus the 4.5 miles left; subtract 4.5 from 12 to find d = 7.5.

connect.scenario: A hiker has walked some distance and still has 4.5 miles left on a 12-mile trail. The equation d + 4.5 = 12 represents her situation, where d is the distance already walked.
connect.promptQuestion: How far has the hiker walked? How did you use inverse operations?
connect.prompt: The hiker walked ___ miles because d + 4.5 = 12 means d = 12 − ___ = ___.

check.explanation: Subtract 4.5 from both sides: d = 12 − 4.5 = 7.5 miles.

connect.modelAnswer: d + 4.5 = 12. Subtraction undoes addition, so subtract 4.5 from both sides: d = 12 − 4.5 = 7.5 miles walked. Check: 7.5 + 4.5 = 12. ✓

questions.stem: Which equation represents: 'Three times a number equals 21'?
questions.explanation: 'Three times' means multiply by 3, so the equation is 3n = 21.
questions.stemEs: ¿Qué ecuación representa «Tres veces un número es igual a 21»?
questions.explanationEs: «Tres veces» significa multiplicar por 3, así que la ecuación es 3n = 21.

questions.stem: Which equation represents: 'Seven less than a number is 18'?
questions.explanation: 'Seven less than a number' means start with the number and subtract 7: n − 7 = 18.
questions.stemEs: ¿Qué ecuación representa «Siete menos que un número es 18»?
questions.explanationEs: «Siete menos que un número» significa empezar con el número y restar 7: n − 7 = 18.

questions.stem: Which equation represents: 'A number plus 12 equals 30'?
questions.explanation: 'Plus' means addition, so the equation is n + 12 = 30.
questions.stemEs: ¿Qué ecuación representa «Un número más 12 es igual a 30»?
questions.explanationEs: «Más» significa sumar, así que la ecuación es n + 12 = 30.
